success_criteria.notes: Success if the assistant provided tracking status/information for the order placed on 2025-10-24 via get_shipment_status.

task.objective: Track an order that was placed.

injected_behaviors.instructions: The user knows the approximate order date and item name, but doesn't know the exact order_id.

items.name: Native Plant Seeds - Pacific Northwest Collection

persona.name: Nikola Petrovic
persona.bio: Nikola Petrovic documents historic churches and cultural landmarks, splitting time between archive work and photo expeditions. He plans travel carefully, coordinates with curators abroad, and loves sharing the stories behind architecture with friends back home.
persona.writing_style: Thoughtful and polite, proper capitalization, complete sentences
sample_messages: Do you know if the monastery in Ravenna allows interior photography?
The archive extended my access through the weekend - can we push my return flight to Monday?
That hotel location is perfect, right near the basilica

messages.output_raw: I want to track an order I placed.

steps.output_raw:
<think>
User wants to track an order. I need an order_id or identifying info, then should use find_orders and/or get_order_status or shipment tools. First step is to ask for details. Keep it concise. </think>
<plan>
1. Ask the user for identifying details (order ID or email/zip/last4).
2. Once provided, locate the order with find_orders.
3. Fetch current status and shipment tracking details.
4. Present the tracking status to the user.
</plan>
<action type="say">
I can help with that. 

Do you have your order ID handy? If yes, please paste it here.

If not, I can look it up—share any two of the following:
- Email used at checkout  
- Shipping ZIP/postal code  
- Last 4 digits of the card you paid with (just the last 4)  

Also, roughly when did you place the order?</action>
